stories.headline: Nearly 1,000 arrested after mass cost-of-living protests and clashes across France

sources.body:
Nearly 1,000 arrests were made as hundreds of thousands of people took part in another day of protests across France which were followed by some clashes late on Saturday, officials have said.

After a day of largely peaceful demonstrations, police fired tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters in a number of cities including Paris, while barricades were set alight in Marseille and people ripped boards from a shop in Bordeaux.

But officials have so far managed to avoid rioting and looting on the scale seen last weekend, which resulted in some of the worst scenes of disorder in France's modern history.

The interior ministry said an estimated 410,000 people protested on Saturday, while the unions put the number at about 800,000.

Some 70,000 police officers were deployed and restrictions imposed in several cities to prevent the latest protests over the cost of living and poor school conditions from descending into the kind of chaos which saw officers outnumbered, hundreds of businesses looted and buildings torched.

President Emmanuel Macron had decreed earlier this week that only demonstrations organised by a recognised trade unions would be permitted. Hundreds of people have been jailed for vandalism, arson and looting after fast-track court hearings in recent days.

Clashes between protesters and riot police in Paris erupted at the end of a peaceful march from the city's Porte d'Italie towards Porte de Vincennes on Saturday, where the police operation included an elite unit that usually deals with organised crime and counter-terrorism.

Some protesters were seen erecting makeshift barricades and pelting officers with projectiles, while police baton-charged groups of masked youths who were smashing the windows of a car dealership.

French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said that "several thousand radical activists gathered at the rear of the march, including around 500 individuals identified as rioters", the AFP news agency reported.

In the southern port of Marseille, rubbish bins were set ablaze and metal sheets used to block streets. A law enforcement vehicle was seen driving through a burning barricade in France's second-largest city.

Meanwhile, some protesters in dark clothing and face coverings were seen taking boards off a building to build a street barricade in the southern city of Bordeaux.

In Lyon, police used tear gas grenades to disperse a crowd which had reportedly gathered in an area deemed off-limits by the local prefecture.

"There were around 150 of us, mostly secondary school and university students. Then the tear gas came almost immediately. You could barely see anything in the street," said one protester in France's third-largest city.

Nuñez said late in the day that nearly 1,000 people had been arrested, a number he said would increase.

The minister also said two people had been "seriously injured": one in the south-western city of Toulouse, and another one in Clermont-Ferrand, central France.

Earlier, a peaceful protester in Paris who gave her name as Zelie told the BBC people had taken to the streets because they were "really frustrated" and had been "suffering a lot" since Macron came to office.
sources.headline: Almost 1,000 arrested as clashes follow another day of mass protests across France

sources.body: Hundreds of thousands marched across France Saturday protesting the rising cost of living. While demonstrations in Paris started peacefully, they ended with a heavy government security response following escalation. Other cities saw clashes that also contributed to the near-1,000 arrested across the country, meanwhile other countries in Europe rallied over issues with some overlap. "The marches went well" said Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez.
sources.headline: 'The marches went well' – French government on demonstrations a week after looting and violence

sources.body:
Almost 1,000 arrested as police charge crowd in Paris and teargas used to stop protesters reaching other city centres

Hundreds of thousands marched in cities across France on Saturday in largely peaceful protests to support schoolchildren’s demands for more teachers and repairs to dilapidated buildings, as Emmanuel Macron faces a social and political crisis in his final months as president.

In Paris, at least 110,000 people marched along the eastern edge of the city, according to government estimates. They supported high schoolers but also complained of the high cost of living and the government’s heavy policing, saying riot police had been sent to target school protesters over the past month, instead of the government offering political solutions.

The mood in Paris on Saturday afternoon was peaceful and lighthearted, with brass bands playing and children and grandchildren present. Some people carried banners critical of the government’s policing, saying: “Oppression breeds rebellion” and “The right to protest”.

But at the end of the Paris demonstration, at Porte de Vincennes on the city’s eastern edge, different groups of masked men dressed in black emerged who had not appeared to have taken part in the peaceful march. Some groups of masked men threw glass bottles and stones at police, who responded with teargas, water cannon and stun grenades. A bin was set alight and fireworks were set off towards police.

Riot police also charged a larger crowd of protesters at the end of the Paris march, using batons against them.

Police fired teargas to prevent protesters in Lyon, Lille, Montpellier, Nantes and Toulouse from reaching city centres. In Marseille, some bin fires were lit amid clashes with police. At least two people were seriously injured, one in Clermont-Ferrand and another in Toulouse, who reportedly had fingers blown off.

The government estimated that at least 400,000 people had marched across France . Trade unions estimated the number at double that. The interior ministry said there had been almost 1,000 arrests.

Laurent Nuñez, the interior minister, said that at various street marches across France there were what he called “high-risk groups” who “broke away from the main body and sought to commit acts of violence”.

More than 70,000 police were on the streets of French cities, with shops boarded up and many museums closed. The government had feared a repeat of last Saturday, when, despite peaceful protests taking place, France saw one of the most violent days of unrest in years, with public buildings burned, hundreds of shops destroyed and looted and at least 2,700 people arrested in cities across the country.

At Saturday’s protests, there was widespread anger at Macron for banning non-union demonstrations that his government deemed “illegitimate” and for keeping all protesters away from city centres.

At the Paris march, Nadège, a 43-year-old communications worker, said she had been teargassed last weekend at a peaceful demonstration. “I’m out again peacefully today to support everyone who is brave enough to demonstrate. It does take courage. People are afraid now. We have to keep our rights alive … In France, it’s our legal right to protest in the street and I’m here to defend that.”
sources.headline: Hundreds of thousands march across France in protests over schools and policing

stories.headline: Brazilian voters choose between Lula and Bolsonaro's son in presidential runoff

sources.body:
Brazilians go to the polls on Sunday to elect their new president in a closely fought run-off election.

The choice is between the 80-year-old incumbent, left-winger Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who is seeking a fourth non-consecutive term in office, and right-wing senator Flávio Bolsonaro, 45.

Bolsonaro is the son of former right-wing president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year prison sentence for plotting a coup after losing the last election in 2022.

This is Bolsonaro's election to lose after he came top in the first round of voting on 4 October, which US President Donald Trump called a "very big" victory.

Never before has a candidate who trailed after the first round managed to overturn the deficit and win in the second round.

Bolsonaro's supporters were jubilant at his final campaign rallies, confident that he would bring change to Brazil through his promised tough crackdown on organised crime, as well as tax and public spending cuts.

He campaigned on the eve of polls in Belo Horizonte, the capital of Minas Gerais, which has been a must-win state for any presidential hopeful since the 1980s.

"The time is almost here," Bolsonaro told supporters in a social media video.

"There are only a few hours left before we shape the future of our nation for the next 30 or 40 years."

He has also pledged to release his father, who is currently serving his sentence under house arrest due to ill health.

In Barra de Tijuca, Rio de Janeiro, where Jair Bolsonaro has a home, Bolsonaro supporters rallied in support of him dressed in the national colours.

"Brazil needs change, and Flávio is the person that represents that today, after so many years of the Left destroying the economy and the country," one told BBC News.

Another said that what she most liked about Flávio Bolsonaro was his promise to "end violence in Brazil, end terrorism, narco-trafficking, and to reduce interest rates".

Since Bolsonaro's first-round victory, supporters of Lula have arranged huge rallies in support of him to try to boost turnout after 33 million people did not cast a vote earlier this month.

On Saturday, Lula told a huge crowd on Rio de Janeiro's Copacabana beach that this election was a matter of "sovereignty" and people would choose between the one who kissed the Brazilian flag or the American flag.

Lula's administration has accused the US of interfering in Brazil's election , an allegation Washington has called "baseless".

"We're going to win the election for one simple reason: it's true that the people want change [but] they want to move forward," he said. "They don't want to go backward."

A supporter called Roberta told BBC News: "This movement is to show we have strength. We've woken up, we're coming to the street to make a difference and turn the vote around."

A man wearing Brazil's national yellow and green football shirt said Bolsonaro supporters had "appropriated" the jersey but Lula supporters were taking it back.

Lula and his Workers' Party have cast this election as a "battle for democracy", arguing that Jair Bolsonaro's conviction for coup-plotting is evidence that "Bolsonarismo" constitutes a threat to Brazil's democratic institutions.
sources.headline: Voters in Brazil to choose between Lula and Bolsonaro's son

sources.body:
The pivotal run-off will determine whether Brazilians stick with their left-wing leader or shift towards the right.

Brazil’s presidential candidates Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro have rallied thousands of supporters in a final show of campaign strength in advance of the country’s closely contested run-off election.

Donning a red hat, Lula addressed hundreds of supporters at Rio de Janeiro’s Copacabana Beach on Saturday, waving a Brazilian flag from a campaign truck as crowds gathered on the final day of campaigning.

“The people must choose either someone who kisses the national flag or someone who kisses the American flag”, the 80-year-old told the crowd as he referenced his opponent’s ties to US President Donald Trump.

Lula is seeking a fourth, non-consecutive term in Sunday’s run-off, which will task Brazilians with determining whether to stick with their incumbent left-wing leader or join a broader regional shift towards the right.

Bolsonaro, a senator and son of former far-right President Jair Bolsonaro, secured 47 percent of the vote in the first round, narrowly ahead of Lula’s 45 percent.

Recent polling shows Lula and the younger Bolsonaro remain about even on the eve of the pivotal election.

A CNT/MDA survey released on Saturday revealed Bolsonaro would receive 46.3 percent of the vote compared ⁠with 45 percent for the left-wing ⁠Lula. Last week, ⁠the poll showed a slightly closer race with Bolsonaro leading ⁠Lula 46.8 percent to ⁠45.9 percent.

The poll’s margin of error was 2.2 ‌percentage ‌points.

On Saturday, Bolsonaro’s supporters, including hundreds of motorcyclists wearing Brazil’s yellow national football shirts, gathered in the southeastern state of Minas Gerais.

One of those supporters, Ebert Dorigo, accused Lula’s Workers’ Party (PT) of encouraging dependence on government welfare, arguing a change in direction was needed for the country.

“The values we uphold are nation and family. Our country is divided today because, due to welfare-based policies, some people … haven’t grasped that improvement and achievement come only through hard work,” he told the news agency AFP.

The bitter campaign has exposed deep divisions over economic policy, crime and Brazil’s political future, which Bolsonaro has pledged to tackle with hundreds of thousands of more spots in prison and cuts to government spending.

His father, who served as president from 2019 to 2022, is serving a 27-year prison sentence for attempting a coup after losing that year’s election to Lula.

The two candidates struck a calmer tone during their final debate on Friday, although they traded accusations over the country’s economic difficulties and their respective records.

For some voters, however, the choice has been a difficult one.

“If there were any other candidate, that would be a better option,” Gabriela Ribeiro Viana, an event organiser, told AFP. “But we’re stuck choosing between the worst, the horrible, and the lesser evil”.
sources.headline: Brazil’s Lula, Bolsonaro draw thousands to election-eve rallies

sources.body:
Nearly 159 million people to head to polls on Sunday in battle between leftwing incumbent and Flávio Bolsonaro

More than one million supporters of Brazil’s leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, have streamed on to Rio’s most famous beach for a giant protest they hope will propel him towards a historic election fightback against his far-right rival, Flávio Bolsonaro .

Nearly 159m Brazilians will vote in the election’s runoff on Sunday, with the pair tied in the polls after Bolsonaro won the first round on 4 October by 47% to 45%.

On Saturday, under a fierce sun, red-clad crowds packed the 2.5-mile Copacabana beach in an attempt to help Lula clinch a dramatic and unprecedented comeback . Never since the return of democracy to Brazil in the 1980s has the first-round loser managed to bounce back.

Josias Silva, a 61-year-old truck driver, voiced confidence that his 80-year-old president, who was first elected in 2002, would win a fourth non-consecutive term. He carried a homemade sign to the carnival-like procession reading: “Lula re-elected. Tomorrow will be a new day.”

“The people have woken up,” Silva said of the large pro-Lula street protests that have swept Brazil since the leftist’s first-round defeat, many led by students.

“Young people know we need this victory because otherwise we will have dictatorship again – and we don’t want dictatorship. We don’t want hatred. We don’t want guns. We want a country of love,” added Silva, celebrating the large number of people who came to witness one of the final presidential campaign rallies in Lula’s storied 50-year political career.

“There’s never been a demonstration like this one. This is the biggest protest in the history of Brazil. And we are going to win tomorrow with more than 60% of the votes,” Silva claimed.

Polls suggest a far tighter margin and most analysts see Bolsonaro, whose father, Jair Bolsonaro, was president from 2019 to 2022 , as the slight favourite, having sold himself to voters as someone who will tackle chronic levels of violent crime with an iron fist.

However, in recent days Lula has appeared to regain the initiative and climb in the polls, amid a succession of scandals involving his rightwing foe. Last week the Brazilian magazine Piauí claimed that at the height of Brazil’s 2020 coronavirus outbreak, Flávio Bolsonaro attended a boat party attended by sex workers and vaccine lobbyists hoping to strike a deal with the government of his father.

Some experts speculate a Lula comeback may be possible. At the Copacabana rally – which Rio’s City Hall said attracted about 1.1 million people – activists unfurled an enormous yellow and green banner declaring: “WE ARE GOING TO TURN THIS AROUND!”

On Saturday afternoon, Lula attended an even larger rally on Paulista Avenue, in the heart of Brazil’s biggest city, São Paulo.

“I’m super excited. Lula’s going to win,” said Marta Moraes, a 59-year-old restaurateur, as she joined Saturday’s demo in Rio.

Moraes said the election was not about left versus right. “We’ve nothing against the right … what we’re against is Bolsonarismo,” she said, tears filling her eyes as she recalled how Flávio Bolsonaro’s father botched the response to Covid during his chaotic 2019-2022 administration.
sources.headline: More than one million Lula supporters rally on eve of Brazilian election runoff

stories.headline: Serbia votes in election pitting its longtime leader against a student-led movement

sources.body:
Polls show populist leader Aleksandar Vucic in a tight race against the anticorruption and anti-authoritarian movement.

Serbians are voting in parliamentary elections amid a mass student protest ⁠movement that seeks to oust longtime populist leader Aleksandar Vucic, who has held power as prime minister and then president for more than a decade.

The snap elections, called by Vucic in September, follow almost two years of student-led demonstrations against perceived corruption ⁠and creeping authoritarianism, triggered by the deaths of 16 people when a train station canopy collapsed in the city of Novi Sad in 2024.

The students have since gained widespread support.

A loss for Vucic ⁠would mark a profound political shift in the Balkan country of some 6 million people, reminiscent of the defeat of Hungary’s Viktor Orban in April.

But Vucic, who resigned as president in September to run again for prime minister, is a strong incumbent. Many voters thank him for pulling Serbia out of economic obscurity and ‌orchestrating a period of sustained modernisation.

“The Serbian election ⁠is shaping up to be a watershed moment for the country as the Student List mounts the biggest challenge against Vucic yet,” Mario Bikarski, senior Europe analyst at risk consultancy Verisk Maplecroft, told the Reuters news agency.

During the campaign, Vucic has promised higher pensions and public sector salaries, investment in state healthcare, and subsidies for young couples. He has balanced closer ties with China, a major investor, and Russia, Serbia’s traditional ally and principal supplier of natural gas, while leaving the door open to joining the European Union.

But relations with the EU have frayed under his leadership, with the bloc growing increasingly frustrated over a lack of reforms addressing the judiciary, the rule of law and corruption.

The Student List movement’s agenda focuses on rooting out corruption and improving schooling, while saying little about their international ambitions.

Their roster of 250 largely unfamiliar candidates, including university professors, actors and farmers, is led by cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic.

Opinion polls are predicting a tight race.

An Ipsos poll published on Thursday gives Vucic’s Serbian Progressive Party 47 percent ⁠of the vote to the students’ 40 percent, though other polls have put the students ahead.

Rights groups and activists say repression has worsened since the deadly train station canopy collapse, which was widely blamed on government corruption and sparked the student demonstrations.

About 150,000 supporters of the student movement rallied in central Belgrade on Thursday.

Vucic and his party have repeatedly denied accusations of repression, corruption and spying on their opponents.

The former president claims the students are funded by foreign agents in Croatia and Montenegro, a charge the students deny.
sources.headline: Serbia votes in election pitting longtime leader against student movement

stories.headline: Israeli forces displace more than 2,000 Palestinians in Hebron after attack on soldiers

sources.body: The Palestinian Authority called for international pressure on Israel after a Palestinian official said around 1,200 Palestinians in Hebron in the West Bank were forced to leave their homes following an attack on Friday which killed two Israeli soldiers. Israeli defence minister Israel Katz later confirmed in an interview that the displacements had reached the 2,000 mark.
sources.headline: Israeli forces displace 2,000 Palestinians in Hebron after deadly attack on soldiers

sources.body:
Palestinians in Hebron are ‘living in fear’ with the city closed, while Israeli forces arrest dozens across the West Bank.

Israel has imposed a lockdown and displaced thousands of Palestinians from their homes in Hebron, as the military conducts raids in the occupied West Bank following the deaths of two Israeli soldiers.

This comes as the Palestinian Authority on Saturday called for international pressure on Israel to protect Hebron’s residents, who said soldiers announced forced evacuation orders over loudspeakers late at night, leaving them with no time to prepare and few places to move to.

Hebron’s Mayor Yousef al-Ja’bari told Al Jazeera on Saturday that 2,200 people had been forced from their homes by Israeli troops and raids.

Later on Saturday, Israel’s defence minister confirmed that “about 2,000” people have been displaced. “They will not be allowed to return to their neighbourhood until we’ve finished dealing with all the Hamas issues in Hebron,” Israel Katz said in an interview with public broadcaster Kan.

Hundreds of Israeli raids have taken place since Friday’s attack by two Palestinian gunmen on an Israeli army reserve base, which killed two Israeli soldiers. The two Palestinians were also killed.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered a “full lockdown” of the occupied West Bank following the attack.

Mayor al-Ja’bari told Al Jazeera that Hebron residents can neither enter nor leave the city.

Israeli soldiers also fired a stun grenade at Al Jazeera journalists near the Farsh al-Hawa checkpoint in Hebron, as the journalists documented an Israeli operation to bulldoze homes and vehicles in the area.

The Israeli military carried out raids across at least 15 areas of the occupied West Bank on Saturday, Al Jazeera correspondents on the ground reported.

The targeted areas include Jenin and Nablus in the north; Ramallah, el-Bireh, Birzeit, and occupied East Jerusalem in the centre; and Bethlehem in the south.

The Palestinian Prisoner’s Society said Israeli forces arrested about 70 Palestinians in the raids.

Raids in several towns in the Jenin governorate on Saturday evening injured two people, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.

Sources told Wafa that two others were injured in separate incidents southeast and east of Jenin.

The Palestinian Red Crescent said early on Sunday that it had treated nine people, including six children, for “suffocation” after Israeli soldiers fired tear gas in Halhul, north of Hebron.

According to a statement early on Sunday, the Israeli military will bar Palestinian workers from entering most areas of the West Bank on Sunday through Monday, and a full closure of crossings into and out of the West Bank will be enforced on Tuesday, the day of the Israeli elections.

The Palestinian Authority, which governs some of the West Bank, called Israel’s actions “collective punishment” , citing the demolition of homes, forced displacement of entire neighbourhoods, and the “closure and siege of Palestinian cities”, and urged the international community to intervene, Wafa reported.
sources.headline: More than 2,000 forced from homes in Hebron amid Israel’s West Bank raids

stories.headline: Justice Department seeks to preemptively block Alaska Senate result if Republican incumbent loses

sources.body: President Donald Trump is escalating his crusade to exert control of America’s elections as his party barrels towards a potentially bruising midterm. The Justice Department has already filed lawsuits in nearly every state to try and gain access to voter files. Trump revisited his longstanding bid to restrict mail voting, sparking a legal battle that reached the Supreme Court. He sought to make anti-terrorism funds for state and local governments contingent on how they administer elections. He has threatened to withhold federal election funding from states that refuse to change voter registration forms and sparred with Republican lawmakers over a bill to overhaul elections. But with most of those efforts stalling, on Thursday, just 12 days before Election Day, the DOJ took things even further: In an extraordinary move, it asked a court to preemptively block Alaska’s Senate results if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses, stunning current and former election officials in both parties. “Boy, they are scraping the bottom of the barrel. It feels like a real desperation play to me, because it has got zero basis in the law,” said Ben Ginsberg, a veteran Republican election law expert who was counsel to George W. Bush’s 2000 and 2004 presidential campaigns. At virtually every corner, courts have rebuffed Trump’s efforts, and legal experts expect the latest DOJ maneuver to have the same outcome. The requests for voter rolls were blocked repeatedly by members of Trump’s own party and struck down in court . The attempt to restrict mail voting was ultimately blocked by the Supreme Court. Federal judges blocked both the anti-terrorism and election funding efforts. The SAVE Act, which would require voters to provide proof of citizenship at the polls, has stalled in the Senate. But Trump keeps pushing, telling reporters Friday that he had personally green-lit the Alaska lawsuit: “I'm the one that said 'Do it.’” The gambit is another sign that Trump is once again ramping up his efforts to exert greater control over how elections are administered — with officials bracing for what may come next. “I think there is an attempt to lay a foundation to say, ‘If we had won these lawsuits, we would have won the election,’” Gabriel Sterling, a Republican and former senior Georgia elections official who sparred with Trump over his false claims of fraud in the state in 2020, said of the Alaska lawsuit. “So, for them, filing and losing for them is the same difference, tactically speaking, potentially.” Trump has been claiming elections were being stolen from him since the 2016 primaries , and his wide-ranging legal and political attempts to overturn his 2020 election loss sparked a riot at the U.S. Capitol in January 2021, even as some in his party want him to move on . “The federal government is his company, and he gets to call all the shots of his company, and that's just never how it's been done before,” said Stephen Richer, Maricopa County, Arizona’s former GOP chief election official. POLITICO reached out to the offices of every Republican statewide election official in America for a response to the DOJ’s action in Alaska. Four declined to comment, and the rest did not respond. Their silence shows just how powerful Trump remains in the party, and how few are willing to cross him just days before November’s midterms. "The survival rate politically of people who oppose Donald Trump on this issue is not great if you're Republican,” said Richer, who was ousted by a more conservative Republican in a 2024 primary after defending the county’s 2020 election results against a yearslong campaign from Trump and his allies to try to prove they were rigged . Arizona Democratic Secretary of State Adrian Fontes railed against the DOJ’s lawsuit, accusing the department of “working as the president's lawyers.” “The Department of Justice is acting in a monstrously political way, and it's purely inappropriate, and they lose a lot of credibility by putting their thumb on the scales,” Fontes said in an interview Friday afternoon. “This attempt in Alaska, if it comes to Arizona, will also fail.” The Justice Department, in a statement posted on social media , said "claims that DOJ is trying to stop Alaska’s election are FALSE." Instead, the DOJ argued it was "seeking to protect election integrity, consistent with the National Voter Registration Act (enacted by Congress) and ensure the will of Alaska voters is respected." Washington state Attorney General Nick Brown, a Democrat, described the legal filing in Alaska as “part of a concerted effort to control the election and to try to dictate the outcome in Donald Trump and the Republican Party’s favor.” Brown said he worried the administration would contest the results of the midterms. “That is not hypothetical,” Brown said. “This is what the president has done for years now, and he has the entire power of government, and most importantly, the Department of Justice around elections, acting at his request.” Sterling predicted the effort would backfire on the GOP. “By talking about stolen elections, by talking about cheating, they're suppressing their own vote and they're encouraging the votes of their opponents,” he said. “So tactically, I think it's politically moronic.” The DOJ lawsuit in Alaska comes less than two weeks before a midterm election cycle in which Republicans are bracing for losses across the map . And the Trump administration’s increasing interventions are raising questions about how far his administration intends to go in trying to assert federal authority over elections that by law are run by state and local officials. A current Georgia Republican election official, granted anonymity to discuss internal deliberations around the Alaska lawsuit, said they are prepared to forcefully push back on any action from the federal government. “Bring it on,” the official said. “I think there's zero credible way for any entity, much less the DOJ, to say that the election results in Georgia are suspect.” The lawsuit is the culmination of years of escalating tensions between the federal government and state election officials over election proceedings. In February , a typically staid gathering of the nation’s top election officials turned fiery when Utah Lt. Gov. Deidre Henderson, a Republican and her state’s chief election official, confronted a senior White House aide over the DOJ’s voter roll push. The DOJ “pretty much slandered all of us to publicly claim that secretaries of state are not doing our jobs and that the federal government has to do it for us. Not OK,” Henderson said to White House Deputy Director of Intergovernmental Affairs Jared Borg, as her colleagues and reporters looked on. On Wednesday, Henderson’s office received a letter from the Justice Department informing her that election monitors will be sent to her state. Her office responded the next day by distributing instructions to poll workers noting that the DOJ observers “must not interfere with voting” and giving guidance in case “a situation arises involving law enforcement or legal demands.” Henderson was unsparing in a recent interview with CBS News . "In the past two elections that I oversaw as lieutenant governor the threats were all external," she said. "But now we also have threats coming from within our own government." Lisa Kashinsky contributed to this report.
sources.headline: Facing an electoral wipeout, Trump goes after the system

stories.headline: Obama denounces Trump's 'cruelty and corruption' while campaigning for Democrats

sources.body:
Former President Barack Obama has attacked the Trump administration over the Iran war and high consumer prices as he hit the campaign trail for Democrats ahead of the US midterm elections.

"This election is our last best chance to at least rein in some of the foolishness of this administration," Obama told crowds in Ohio on Saturday.

Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump touted his administration's immigration and tariff policies at a rally in Georgia, telling supporters "we're in the golden age of America".

The midterm elections on 3 November will decide which party controls Congress for the rest of Trump's term, and therefore how easy it is for the president to carry out his plans.

Early voting has already begun and Trump cast his ballot on Saturday in Florida alongside his wife First Lady Melania Trump.

Speaking on Saturday in Ohio and Michigan, Obama targeted Trump and his cabinet members, at one point mocking the president's attempt to redecorate the White House.

"After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which we have not seen in the modern era, you get a chance to say, 'enough is enough,'" the former president said in Cleveland.

Obama said he sympathised with voters who rejected Democrats in 2024 over economic and inflation concerns following the Covid pandemic. But he said Trump had only himself to blame for the current state of the economy.

"If you thought everything was too expensive before 'you know who'," he said, referring to Trump without using his name, "everything is more expensive now".

Trump, meanwhile, acknowledged that oil prices were "temporarily high" but said "our country is getting stronger and stronger all the time, and those pump prices are going to come down".

The Republican president has faced significant pressure to lower fuel prices, which have jumped due to the wars in Iran and Ukraine.

Talking up the economy, Trump told the crowd in Perry "we're taking in massive amounts of money through tariffs", and repeated his pledge to offer every adult American a $5,000 (£3,700) payout if Republicans win both chambers of Congress.

He also took aim at the Democrats, telling the crowd they would "loot your wealth" and "annihilate your borders".

Using derogatory language, he accused the Democrats of trying to open up immigration from Libya, Yemen, Haiti and Somalia - countries which he described as "terror-infested".

Describing a previous meeting with several senators, he recalled: "I said, 'Why do we always have to take people from shithouse countries? Why can't we take people from, like, well... Norway, Sweden? Why not Denmark?'"

In Ohio, the current president faced an attack from his predecessor over the war in Iran, with Obama telling Democrat supporters the conflict had given Tehran "veto power" over the Strait of Hormuz.

When asked about the war earlier in the day, Trump said: "I've done it very effectively and I may have to finish it off, or maybe they'll make a deal, but I'm not sure. Either way, we win."
sources.headline: Obama attacks Trump as he campaigns for Democrats ahead of midterm elections

sources.body:
Former US president says Trump ‘chose to make a series of bad decisions’, highlighting the US-Israel war on Iran.

Barack Obama has criticised the “cruelty and corruption” during US President Donald Trump’s second term, as the former president campaigned for Democratic candidates in two Midwestern states.

Obama delivered scathing criticism of Trump on Saturday at a midterm election campaign rally in Ohio, slamming his successor’s foreign policies.

“The current president chose to make a series of bad decisions,” the 65-year-old Democrat said in Cleveland. “Most importantly, he decided to start an unnecessary war that nobody asked for,” he added, referring to the US-Israel war on Iran.

Obama urged Ohioans to vote against the Republican administration, saying: “After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which we have not seen in the modern era, you get a chance to say, ‘Enough is enough’.”

Later on Saturday evening, Obama headed to Michigan to campaign for Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and Democratic gubernatorial candidate Jocelyn Benson.

At the Detroit rally, he framed the November 3 vote as a “circuit breaker” to “at least rein in some of the foolishness” of Trump’s presidency. “We have never seen a president excel in straight-up grifting, ⁠on your dime, like this,” Obama said.

“Never seen a president so intent ⁠on selling favours like this,” he also said, adding that the Republican Party “seems to stand for corrupt government, or inept government, or no government”.

Obama ridiculed the Trump ⁠administration’s claims of victory against Iran. He argued that the war has given Iran more economic leverage because its threats to attack shipping in the Strait of Hormuz have unsettled oil exporters.

“Iran now has veto power over the Strait of Hormuz, ‌where oil goes through to get to the world,” Obama said.

The former president also addressed the recent controversy in Ohio’s gubernatorial race surrounding an attack advertisement by Republican candidate Vivek Ramaswamy against Democrat Amy Acton.

“In recent days, we’ve seen there is no line he will not cross, no low he will not sink to,” Obama said of Ramaswamy. “I don’t know what’s happened where the standards of behaviour are so low that somebody could run an ad like that.”

In the advertisement, Donna Arthur, Acton’s mother, disputes her daughter’s account of a childhood involving homelessness and ⁠⁠⁠⁠sexual abuse by her stepfather, urging Ohioans not to vote for her.

Acton says she has not seen her mother since 1978. Acton’s brother has supported her account of being sexually abused by her stepfather when she was a child. The stepfather, who died in 2004, was charged with rape.

Obama backed Acton, saying that she has “spoken movingly about her painful childhood and all she’s experienced: abuse, neglect and homelessness”.

The former president shared the rally stage with Acton and Ohio’s former Democratic senator, Sherrod Brown.

Trump defended the Ramaswamy advertisement on Saturday, when he cast his ballot early in Florida.
sources.headline: Obama slams Trump’s ‘cruelty and corruption’ as he rallies Democrats

stories.headline: New York Archdiocese agrees to pay $800 million to 1,300 sexual-abuse survivors

sources.body:
The settlement is the second-largest after an $880m ​deal reached by the Archdiocese of Los ​Angeles in 2024.

The Archdiocese of New York has agreed to pay more than $800m to settle the legal claims of about 1,300 survivors of sexual abuse by clergy.

New York Archbishop Ronald Hicks said on Saturday that the settlement will be formally signed on November 6 after an agreement with the plaintiffs and their lawyers.

“We are on the verge of being able to, please God, bring some measure of healing and reconciliation to all victim-survivors,” he wrote in an email sent to his priests and shared by the archdiocese’s news outlet.

“This agreement will also allow the archdiocese to turn its full attention once again to its mission of preaching the Gospel, healing the sick, caring for the poor and needy, welcoming the stranger, and educating our children,” he added.

According to The New York Times, which broke the story, each of the approximately 1,300 survivors will receive at least $250,000 from the Archdiocese of New York and potentially more depending on the severity of the abuse suffered.

The settlement is the second-largest of its kind after an $880m deal reached by the Archdiocese of Los Angeles in 2024.

“The unanimous agreement of survivors who filed claims against the Archdiocese of New York marks a powerful moment in the pursuit of justice,” Jeff Anderson, a lawyer representing people who filed more than 1,000 claims against the Catholic Church in New York state, said in a statement.

“Through their courage, sacrifice, and determination, survivors have helped bring about a reckoning and a meaningful step toward accountability.”

The agreement marks the end of years of negotiations with lawyers representing the plaintiffs, as the Catholic Church in the United States has been mired in sexual abuse scandals since the early 2000s.

In the 2000s, media investigations revealed that Catholic priests in the US had committed sexual abuse against thousands of children over several decades, and that church leaders had often covered up these cases or transferred the offending priests instead of reporting them to civil authorities.

Dioceses across the country have had to pay hundreds of millions of dollars in damages, and programmes have been created to compensate survivors without going to trial.

In June, the Archdiocese of San Francisco announced it had reached an agreement to pay $395m to about 530 survivors of sexual abuse committed by its clergy to settle their lawsuits.
sources.headline: New York Archdiocese agrees to pay $800m to 1,300 sexual abuse survivors

La secretaria general del PSOE andaluz, María Jesús Montero, y el secretario general del PSOE y presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, en un mitin en Dos Hermanas (Sevilla). / María José López / Europa Press

El candidato del PSOE en las elecciones generales del 29N, Pedro Sánchez , ha anunciado este sábado que la próxima legislatura, si sigue gobernando el Partido Socialista , reformará y blindará el derecho al aborto en la Constitución española . "Ya les adelanto al PP y Vox que sobre el derecho y el cuerpo de las mujeres ningún hombre volverá jamás a opinar ni a controlarlo", ha asegurado en un mitin en Granada, después de que esta semana el candidato popular, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, haya sugerido la posibilidad de recuperar el consentimiento paterno en chicas de 16 años.

Sánchez ha comenzado su discurso reivindicando la España del poeta granadino Federico García Lorca que, según sus palabras, es "la España que no tiene miedo a su cultura", "la que no borra su memoria", "la que abraza al diferente", "la España humanista, solidaria, universal" y por la que "merece la pena seguir luchando". El presidente del Gobierno ha contado que el biógrafo de Lorca, Ian Gibson , le envió un correo para sugerirle que incorporase al poeta, de plena actualidad por la película 'La Bola Negra' de Los Javis, a sus discursos.

Y eso ha hecho el dirigente socialista en su intervención en la Sala Federico García Lorca del Palacio de Congresos de la capital granadina, en la que ha leído el poema Cantos Nuevos y en la que ha destacado de Lorca que "habló de amores no correspondidos , de personas que no podían vivir como ellas querían, de empatía y de proximidad ante aquellas personas que sufrían". A continuación, ha afirmado que estas elecciones van de elegir "entre solidaridad y egoísmo" y "entre amor y odio": " Os pido que os movilicéis el 29 noviembre para votar progresismo porque no hace falta ser pensionista para reivindicar unas pensiones dignas , ni ser gay para defender los derechos LGTBI . No hace falta ser mujer para reivindicar la igualdad de hombres y mujeres, ni ser ucraniano o palestino para reivindicar el fin de la guerra y los derechos humanos".

El secretario general del PSOE ha contrapuesto así los planteamientos progresistas de su partido frente a los "recortes" que proponen el Partido Popular y Vox en materias como la sanidad, las bajas laborales, el salario mínimo interprofesional, las pensiones o la eutanasia , según ha enumerado, y ha lamentado que pese a que "no llevan ni tres semanas de campaña, su lista de recortes es interminable". "No proponen alternancia, sino involución y ya lo estamos viendo allí donde gobiernan", ha añadido, tras tachar de "censura" la medida de la Junta de Castilla y León , gobernada por los dos partidos de derechas, de dejar de subvencionar películas que estén "ideologizadas".

En este punto, ha recordado la visita esta semana del presidente argentino, Javier Milei , a España para asegurar que "la derecha (española) pertenece al mismo club de la motosierra, los tijeretazos y los recortes" que Milei. Y se ha preguntado "si lo de Feijóo es insolvencia o sectarismo" tras escucharle hablar de una forma "frágil" de cuestiones "importantes para la gente" como la vivienda o el feminismo . Sánchez hizo referencia en este caso a las palabras de Feijóo esta semana en las que afirmó que un ticket de haber pedido una pizza serviría para no echar a un okupa de una vivienda y que se considera feminista porque se había criado entre mujeres. "Ser feminista es no recortar el derecho a las mujeres", ha puntualizado Sánchez ante los presentes, entre los que se encontraba el cantautor granadino, Miguel Ríos.

stories.headline: AI-generated campaign videos intensify Spain's election battle

sources.body:
La campaña para las elecciones generales del 29N aún no ha comenzado, arranca el 13 de noviembre, pero desde que Pedro Sánchez anunció la fecha, los principales partidos políticos ya están en 'modo electoral'. En el ecosistema digital no hay tregua. Uno ataca y el otro responde. Hemos analizado las distintas estrategias de los candidatos y sus organizaciones en las redes sociales con varios expertos en comunicación política. Todos ellos ven un mismo patrón: más contenidos de humor, más uso de la inteligencia artificial y, sobre todo, más agresividad contra el adversario político.

Sánchez se besa con su mujer en un acto del PSOE. Minutos después, el PP transforma con IA esa foto en un beso con José Luis Ábalos, la sube a X y logra casi tres millones de visualizaciones: "La foto de la campaña ".

Mensaje en X del PSOE con el beso de Sánchez y su mujer y respuesta del PP generada con IA.  VerificaRTVE

"Sí, soy zurdo" , proclama el presidente en un video ante la visita del presidente argentino Javier Milei a España, en el que enumera los logros de su Gobierno, y que se ha compartido más de 10.000 veces. El PP responde con un vídeo generado con IA con Begoña Gómez, Ábalos, Koldo o Santos Cerdán, entre otros, compartido más de 7.000 veces.

El presidente también rescata su famoso tuit de la pizzería 'luna rosa', publicado en 2010, después de que Alberto Núñez Feijóo relacionara un ticket de pizza con la okupación .

"Apreciamos un endurecimiento del tono, especialmente en X y en los intercambios entre PP y PSOE ", indican a VerificaRTVE los politólogos Juanma Barrios y Fran Ruiz, del proyecto de divulgación 'El Patio Político '. Creen que la polarización "ya estaba presente en 2023", pero ahora hay un "mayor protagonismo de la burla y la descalificación personal en las cuentas oficiales de los grandes partidos". Y con un elemento adicional: "Sin duda, es la campaña electoral de la IA ", subraya Eva Campos, profesora de Periodismo y Comunicación Política en la Universidad Complutense de Madrid.

Javier Ábrego, experto en marketing digital y creador de la herramienta TweetElecciones.com , aprecia una mayor polarización y agresividad en redes sociales respecto a anteriores campañas: "Por supuesto que sí. Si vemos los tuits más virales de los partidos, los que más se comparten o se ven, son todos ataques al rival ".

Una de las publicaciones del PP más compartidas en X desde que se convocaron las elecciones es una mofa de una lesión en el cuádriceps que sufrió Óscar Puente en 2023: "Miedo le tenías tú a un esguince" . El ministro respondió con el siguiente mensaje : "Son la peor gentuza que habita este país. Por cierto, me rompí la rodilla trabajando, cosa que no hace el vago al que habéis puesto en la alcaldía".

Es un caso que, según los fundadores de 'El Patio Político' , muestra que "la discusión deja de girar sobre decisiones públicas y se centra en una circunstancia personal". No es el meme en sí lo que endurece la campaña, sino convertir la humillación del adversario en su contenido ", explican.
sources.headline: Del mitin al meme: la inteligencia artificial para atacar al adversario agita la batalla electoral del 29N

VIGO, 24/10/2026.- El presidente del Partido Popular, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, participa en un acto este sábado en VIgo. EFE/ Salvador Sas

El presidente del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, se ha referido este sábado al de Pedro Sánchez como “el Gobierno de la corrupción” y ha advertido que, si llega a la Moncloa tras el 29N, no va a “indultar a los corruptos”: “Me encargaré de que paguen por todo”, ha garantizado.

En Vigo, ante un auditorio repleto que ha ovacionado en varias ocasiones al candidato popular, Núñez Feijóo ha enumerado ”17 sumarios abiertos” que afectan al Partido Socialista, en los que “se acusa de 23 delitos”, con ”131 imputados” y penas que, según el código penal, podrían superar los 1.000 años de cárcel, ha dicho. “Eso es lo que les ha motivado a adelantar las elecciones”, ha aseverado.

Tras lamentar que “los currantes sean los que tienen que pagar la mordida de los corruptos”, Núñez Feijóo se ha referido también al caso Zapatero. “Todavía estamos esperando a que nos expliquen de dónde salieron las joyas”, ha dicho, antes de exigir al expresidente socialista que “se lo explique al juez” y “que pida perdón a los españoles por las lecciones que nos quiso dar y por la vergüenza que nos hace pasar”.

El presidente del PP ha mencionado durante el mitin de precampaña a Pedro Sánchez, José Luis Ábalos, Sántos Cerdán o Leire Díez para advertirles de que “todo tendrá consecuencias, todo”. “Me encargaré de que paguen por todo”, ha dicho, “a los corruptos no los vamos a indultar”.

El candidato del PP al 29-N, Xavier Garcia Albiol, ha afirmado que “la mayoría” de okupas son “unos caraduras”, por lo que ha prometido que el PP les aplicará la ley “de la forma más dura posible y con todas las consecuencias”. Por su parte, el líder del PP en Barcelona, ​​Daniel Sirera, ha asegurado que, “por culpa de los tres gobiernos socialistas”, la ciudad se ha convertido en la capital europea de “la delincuencia, el empleo y la degradación” y ha exigido al presidente de la Generalitat, Salvador Illa, y al alcalde de Barcelona, ​​Jaume Collboni, que desalojen la acampada de plaça Catalunya. Albiol y Sirera han estado acompañados del presidente de la Junta, Juanma Moreno, y del vicesecretario de Coordinación Autonómica y Local y Análisis Electoral del PP, Elías Bendodo, cabeza de lista por Málaga al Congreso. Bendodo ha afirmado que cuando el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, llegó a Moncloa, la vivienda era el “problema número 16 de los españoles” y que en la actualidad es el primero. “Con el PSOE el precio de la vivienda en nuestro país ha subido un 74% y el alquiler un 44%. Las ocupaciones se han disparado”, ha dicho.

Feijóo ha afirmado que se siente “preparado” para ganar, pero ha advertido que esa meta “no es fácil porque, a un lado y a otro, el objetivo es que el PP no tenga el resultado que merece España”.

Después de repartir abrazos y saludos con la canción 'Hall of fame' (Salón de la fama) de fondo, ha subido a la tribuna con gritos de “presidente, presidente” y ha construido su discurso en torno al éxito del PP en Galicia, donde gobierna desde 2009.

Catalunya. “Una cosa son les protestes i una altra la violencia gratuïta. Pot ser un efecte mirall que copia altres capitals europees. Però aquí la resposta serà contundent ”, ha deixat clar la responsable d’Interior. Foto: ACN El centre de Barcelona ha viscut durant la tarda i el vespre aldarulls i moments de tensió per una protesta juvenil, amb contenidors cremats , saquejos a comerços, aparadors de diverses botigues trencats i destrosses al mobiliari urbà . Els Mossos d’Esquadra han desplegat un ampli dispositiu policial als entorns de la plaça de Catalunya, on s’han concentrat els fets. La protesta ha començat a primera hora de la tarda i segons fonts policials no havia estat comunicada. A mesura que avançava el vespre ha anat creixent en nombre i també ha anat pujant la tensió. Les primeres càrregues policials s’han produït a la tarda després del llançament d’alguns objectes com pedres i ampolles contra el cordó policial. Els manifestants eren sobretot joves que apuntaven que s’han mobilitzat responent a una crida que segueix l’ onada de protestes que sacseja Europa . La concentració s’ha convocat a través de les xarxes socials. Fonts dels Mossos han explicat a betevé que ha estat una protesta no autoritzada , ja que no s’havia comunicat l’organització de cap mobilització al centre de la ciutat. Els Mossos d’Esquadra han assegurat que “ grups violents de persones amb la cara tapada ” han cremant contenidors, han vandalitzat mobiliari urbà i han llançat pedres contra la policia. També et pot interessar Una “rebel·lia autèntica”: què hi ha darrere l’onada de protestes i aldarulls que sacseja Europa? Andrea Cuerva Bonich 2 minuts de lectura Talls de trànsit i comerços tancats Davant d’aquesta situació, molts establiments i comerços del centre de la ciutat han optat per tancar abans i abaixar la persiana per evitar els desperfectes. La Guàrdia Urbana ha fet talls de trànsit als entorns de la plaça i també s’han tancat alguns dels accessos al metro. Els Ferrocarrils de la Generalitat i els trens de Rodalies han evitat parar a la plaça de Catalunya, seguint indicacions dels Mossos d’Esquadra. De fet, la gran presència d’agents de la policia catalana i de la Guàrdia Urbana, que també s’ha desplegat a la zona, ha sorprès molts vianants i turistes que hi havia a la zona, perquè no constava que hi hagués cap manifestació ni cap acte previstos. L’acampada es desvincula de la protesta de joves Els activistes de l’ acampada s’han desvinculat d’aquesta concentració i de qualsevol acte violent i han assegurat que no es fan responsables del que passi fora . En declaracions a betevé, Kiara Monrroy, membre del col·lectiu, ha explicat que han decidit limitar l’accés a la mobilització i protegir-se amb tanques per seguretat. També et pot interessar L’acampada de la plaça de Catalunya per l’habitatge, protegida amb tanques per “amenaces feixistes” Fàtima Ortí Pablo Mena 1 minut de lectura
sources.headline: Un centenar de detinguts, 25 menors, pels aldarulls al centre de Barcelona: “No quedarà impune”

sources.body:
Aldarulls i saquejos al centre de Barcelona aquest dissabte al vespre, després que una protesta de joves derivés en enfrontaments de grups violents amb la policia, vehicles tombats i mobiliari urbà cremat. Hi ha almenys cent detinguts, una quarta part dels quals menors d'edat, segons ha confirmat la consellera d'Interior, Núria Parlon , en una compareixença amb l'alcalde de la ciutat, Jaume Collboni.

Tant la consellera com l'alcalde han condemnat la violència. Núria Parlon ha dit que en aquests aldarulls hi han participat unes 500 persones "no organitzades" que han vandalitzat una quinzena de comerços del centre de la ciutat, a partir de les sis de la tarda. Parlon ha assegurat que aquests actes no responen a cap reivindicació concreta.

Jaume Collboni ha assegurat que aniran al darrere dels "culpables i causants d'aquests fets", tant dels adults com dels "responsables legals dels menors" que hi han participat. L'Ajuntament "es personarà per defensar els béns públics que han estat vandalitzats", ha afegit.

"Que no pensin que això acabarà aquí. Tindrà conseqüències per als majors d'edat i també per als progenitors dels menors d'edat", ha dit l'alcalde, tant a nivell judicial com patrimonial , ha afegit.

Això no quedarà impune. Anirem fins al final.

La consellera d'Interior ha explicat que possiblement hi haurà més detencions al llarg de la nit, perquè el dispositiu encara està obert. Hi participen més de 210 agents dels Mossos , inclosos 30 agents de la BRIMO, amb el suport de la Guàrdia Urbana i els Bombers, que han apagat 33 punts de foc al centre de la ciutat. També hi ha hagut una quinzena d'agents ferits .

Parlon ha afegit que no es tracta de grups organitzats, sinó de gent que s'ha dedicat a fer destrosses:

És gent desorganitzada que s'ha dedicat a fer actes vandàlics i violència.

"Un pot tenir ràbia, estar en contra de les injustícies, però res del que ha passat a Barcelona té a veure amb això", ha dit Parlon, que ha dit que episodis com aquest deslegitimitzen les reivindicacions dels moviments que es mobilitzen amb respecte.

"Hem de garantir el dret a la manifestació, a la protesta i la llibertat d'expressió. Però hem de garantir que ningú vandalitza ni atemoreix la gent ni trenca vidres ni roba botigues", ha dit l'alcalde.

"El que ha passat avui a Barcelona és violència gratuïta i vandalisme. No té res a veure amb l'acampada", ha insistit l'alcalde de Barcelona. Collboni ha coincidit amb Parlon que hi pot haver un efecte mirall amb protestes d'altres països, com les que s'estan fent a França , però que això no justifica la violència. I que feia dies que veien convocatòries a les xarxes socials que els han permès desplegar els dispositius policials que hi havia sobre el terreny i retirar "objectes o mobiliari urbà que pogués ser utilitzat pels grups violents".

També s'han reforçat els serveis de neteja de cara a aquest diumenge.

Renfe ha tancat l'estació de Plaça Catalunya, on no paren els trens de Rodalies. Els Ferrocarrils de la Generalitat tampoc paren a plaça Catalunya. Segons han informat en un missatge a X, seguint recomanacions dels Mossos, la línia S1 Barcelona-Vallès comença i acaba a l'estació de Provença.
sources.headline: Un centenar de detencions pels aldarulls i saquejos d'aquest dissabte al centre de Barcelona

stories.headline: Catalan education assembly approves a new strike cycle beginning November 26

sources.body:
L'Assemblea Educativa de Catalunya (AEC) ha acordat iniciar un cicle de vagues, que es preveu allargar fins a inicis del segon trimestre. La primera jornada d'aturades serà el dijous 26 de novembre.

El col·lectiu, que també s'adhereix a la vaga general de l'11 de novembre, ha convocat una manifestació el dissabte dia 21 de novembre.

L'AEC s'ha reunit aquest dissabte a Lleida per treballar un calendari de futures mobilitzacions . Aquesta assemblea recull l'opinió dels representants dels centres educatius i es coordina amb els sindicats.

El col·lectiu s'ha reunit a dos quarts d'onze del matí en una aula del campus de Cappont de la Universitat de Lleida.

L'AEC situa com a prioritats per aturar les mobilitzacions l'increment de la plantilla de docents, més recursos per a l'educació inclusiva, una baixada de les ràtios i noves condicions salarials, entre altres reclamacions.

Asseguren que el curs "continua igual" que l'any passat , en què ja hi va haver molta conflictivitat pels recursos que es destinen a l'educació.

La data del dijous 26 de novembre cau en plena campanya electoral i just abans del cap de setmana de les eleccions del 29N .

En el marc de la reunió, l'AEC també ha explicat que es mantenen suspeses les sortides, excursions i colònies durant el curs escolar.

La trobada de l'assemblea arriba l'endemà de la consulta que es va fer al sector, on el 50,2% dels professionals van votar en contra de fer més vagues . Un 80% sí que van votar a favor d'una nova manifestació. La consulta va tenir la participació d'un terç dels mestres, professors i personal d'administració. 32.845 persones van votar.

Amb aquest resultat tan ajustat, els sindicats van optar per proposar una manifestació i una aturada d'un dia .

L'AEC considera que el govern de la Generalitat va fer una "interpretació distorsionada" de la consulta, en considerar que anunciava "la desmobilització del col·lectiu". Asseguren que hi va haver "problemes tècnics" i que l'enquesta no va arribar "a la gran majoria del col·lectiu, davant la mala gestió dels correus de part del Departament".

Aquesta setmana vinent, es reuniran els sindicats i l'Assemblea Educativa per coordinar les pròximes accions .
sources.headline: L'Assemblea Educativa aprova un nou cicle de vagues, amb una primera aturada el 26 de novembre

sources.body:
Decenas de profesores manifestándose en las puertas de la conselleria de Educació

La Assemblea Educativa de Catalunya (AEC) ha acordado convocar una manifestación el sábado 21 de noviembre e iniciar un ciclo de huelgas que se prevé que se prolongue hasta principios del segundo trimestre, con una primera jornada de paros el jueves 26 de noviembre. Así se ha decidido en el debate celebrado en Lleida con representantes de todo el colectivo educativo de distintos puntos del país.

La AEC establece como prioridades para poner fin a las movilizaciones el aumento de la plantilla docente, más recursos para la educación inclusiva, una reducción de las ratios en las aulas y nuevas condiciones salariales, entre otras medidas. En el marco de la reunión, la AEC también ha ratificado mediante una votación su decisión de mantener suspendidas las salidas, excursiones y colonias durante el curso escolar.

La AEC ha hecho un llamamiento al sector para “seguir luchando” mediante la convocatoria de nuevas movilizaciones, además de la huelga general prevista para el 11 de noviembre. En un manifiesto, la Asamblea Educativa ha constatado que “el curso continúa igual” y ha criticado que la consejera de Educación, Ester Niubó, “no quiere dialogar con el colectivo educativo”.

La convocatoria de nuevas jornadas de huelga llega en un momento en el que el apoyo a esta medida de presión se encuentra dividido. Según los resultados de una consulta impulsada por USTEC junto con otros sindicatos contrarios al pacto educativo, la mitad de los docentes prefiere dejar de lado las huelgas y apostar por otras formas de protesta. En cambio, ocho de cada diez participantes se muestran favorables a organizar una manifestación para reclamar una educación pública con más recursos.

En la consulta participaron 32.845 profesionales, una cifra que representa aproximadamente el 30 % de los trabajadores del sector. En concreto, el 50,2 % rechazaron continuar con las jornadas de huelga, frente al 49,8 % que se mostró favorable a mantenerlas. Estos resultados reflejan una caída considerable del apoyo a esta medida de presión: las 16.358 personas que han votado a favor de continuar con las huelgas quedan muy lejos de las cerca de 40.000 que respaldaron esta opción en la última consulta, celebrada en junio.

El resultado se produce después de un intenso ciclo de protestas durante el último trimestre del curso pasado, con 23 jornadas de paro. Además, la huelga del primer día del curso actual tuvo un seguimiento mucho menor, lo que llevó a los sindicatos a consultar al profesorado sobre su estado de ánimo y su grado de compromiso con las medidas de presión planteadas.

Pese al rechazo mayoritario a continuar con las huelgas, el colectivo ha decidido finalmente convocar nuevas jornadas de paro. La representante de la AEC, Elisabet Serra, ha explicado que la consulta “no llegó a muchos trabajadores y trabajadoras”, mientras que también ha defendido la representatividad territorial y sectorial de las asambleas de la organización, como la celebrada este sábado en Lleida.
sources.headline: La Assemblea Educativa convoca una protesta para el 21 de noviembre y un nuevo ciclo de huelgas

stories.headline: Barcelona will offer €400 subsidies for electric bicycles bought from December

sources.body:
Una persona circula con una bicicleta eléctrica / KBO BIKE

El Ayuntamiento de Barcelona ha dado luz verde a la tramitación de las bases que regularán las convocatorias de ayudas de hasta 800 euros por la compra de bicicletas eléctricas , cuya aprobación definitiva está prevista para finales de noviembre. Sin embargo, aunque el plazo de solicitudes no se abrirá hasta principios de 2027, los barceloneses y los autónomos o empresas con domicilio social en la ciudad podrán beneficiarse si han realizado la compra a partir del 1 de diciembre de 2026 .

Los beneficiados podrán recibir 400 euros por la adquisición de bicicletas eléctricas urbanas y el importe ascenderá hasta los 800 euros para las de carga (o 'cargobicis'), con un límite del 40% del precio de adquisición. El plan tiene como objetivo impulsar el transporte verde y contempla una inversión de 4 millones de euros , repartidos a partes iguales a lo largo de cuatro años, con los que se prevé subvencionar unas 8.000 bicicletas urbanas y 800 de carga.

Entre los requisitos figura que la bicicleta sea nueva y esté equipada con timbre, luces y reflectantes , además de contar con una potencia máxima de 250 W, un sistema que corte la asistencia al alcanzar los 25 km/h y un motor que solo se active al pedalear. También será obligatoria su inscripción en el registro de bicicletas de la Xarxa de Ciutats per la Bicicleta , conocido como Biciregistro. En cuanto a los beneficiarios, las personas físicas solo podrán recibir la ayuda una vez, mientras que las personas jurídicas podrán solicitarla para un máximo de cinco vehículos.

"Queremos que la bicicleta sea una opción para los desplazamientos diarios de cada vez más personas y sabemos que el precio es una barrera para muchos", ha explicado Laia Bonet, primera teniente de alcalde, en declaraciones a medios. Por ello, las subvenciones buscan reducir el desembolso que supone adquirir los vehículos para desplazamientos habituales y animar a quienes todavía se lo estén pensando.

"Son medidas que contribuyen a que la decisión de movernos en bici sea más sencilla ", ha señalado. Un objetivo que también pasa por mejorar las infraestructuras y consolidar una red ciclista cada vez más conectada y segura en una ciudad donde el uso de la bicicleta ha crecido un 88% en la última década, hasta alcanzar los 174.887 desplazamientos diarios en 2025, según datos del consistorio.

Carril bici muy transitado en Barcelona. / periodico

La medida se enmarca en la apuesta municipal por consolidar la bicicleta como una alternativa de transporte habitual . En paralelo, la ciudad continúa ampliando y conectando su red ciclista, que cuenta con 270 kilómetros de carriles bici y hasta 1.200 kilómetros de vías ciclables. Asimismo, se ha reforzado el servicio de Bicing con cerca de un millar de bicicletas nuevas, hasta alcanzar las 8.000 unidades, y con un aumento progresivo de los modelos eléctricos.

Con estas ayudas, el Ayuntamiento quiere favorecer el acceso a una movilidad más sostenible , impulsar la renovación del parque ciclista y avanzar hacia los objetivos de neutralidad climática como parte su Plan Clima y de la Agenda de la Bicicleta. La primera convocatoria de 2027 marcará el inicio de un programa que se extenderá durante cuatro años y con el que Barcelona aspira a incorporar miles de nuevas bicicletas eléctricas a sus calles.
sources.headline: Barcelona subvencionará con 400 euros las bicicletas eléctricas compradas a partir de diciembre

sources.body:
L’Ajuntament de Barcelona oferirà ajuts de 400 euros a la ciutadania per a la compra d’una bicicleta elèctrica . L’anunci l’ha fet aquest dissabte la primera tinenta d’alcaldia, Laia Bonet . Hi podran optar totes les persones empadronades a la ciutat que comprin un vehicle elèctric a partir de l’1 de desembre. També podran rebre la subvenció les persones jurídiques amb domicili social a Barcelona.

La comissió de govern d’aquest dijous ha aprovat inicialment les bases que regularan la convocatòria de l’ajut. Es preveu que el vistiplau definitiu es pugui donar a finals de novembre i que entri en vigor l’1 de desembre.

El govern de Jaume Collboni planteja dos tipus d’ajuts. D’una banda, s’atorgaran 400 euros per a la compra de bicicletes elèctriques urbanes, i de l’altra, de 800 euros per a les bicicletes de càrrega, les anomenades cargobike , amb un límit màxim de l’ajut de fins al 40% del preu d’adquisició. En el cas de les empreses, Bonet ha posat el focus en pimes i autònoms.

Tot i que podran optar als ajuts les persones que comprin una bicicleta elèctrica des del desembre d’aquest any, la primera convocatòria per sol·licitar-los s’obrirà l’any vinent, ha explicat Bonet, sense concretar el mes. En total, es destinaran fins a quatre milions d’euros els quatre anys vinents, a raó d’un milió anual. L’Ajuntament preveu un abast de 2.000 noves bicis urbanes i 200 noves bicis de càrrega anuals durant els quatre anys vinents.

Els requisits per optar als ajuts obliguen a comprar una bicicleta nova, no de segona mà, amb timbre, llums i reflectants, amb una potència màxima de 250 W, tall d’assistència a la velocitat de 25 km/h i motor actiu només en pedalar. També caldrà inscriure el vehicle al registre de bicicletes de la Xarxa de Ciutats per la Bicicleta, l’anomenat Biciregistro .

Està previst que els ciutadans puguin rebre un únic ajut, mentre que les persones jurídiques podran adquirir un màxim de cinc bicicletes amb dret a la subvenció, ha remarcat Bonet.

Des de l’1 de març, el consistori subvenciona el canvi d’un ciclomotor de combustió per un d’elèctric. L’import de l’ajut és de 600 euros, amb un pressupost total d’uns 15 milions d’euros. L’executiu socialista estima que es podrien renovar fins a 24.000 vehicles.
sources.headline: L’Ajuntament oferirà ajuts de 400 euros per a la compra d’una bicicleta elèctrica

stories.headline: October rain fills all 15 of Barcelona's stormwater reservoirs for the first time

sources.body:
En només quatre dies, a Barcelona van caure 280 litres per metre quadrat, pràcticament la meitat del que plou en un any. Durant les pluges del 3 i 4 d'octubre , tots els dipòsits pluvials que hi ha repartits per la ciutat es van omplir dues vegades i mitja.

El director general de Barcelona Cicle de l'Aigua, Alejandro Ortiz , ha explicat que no havia passat mai fins ara : "És la primera vegada que s'omplen tots els 15 dipòsits a la vegada".

Són estructures invisibles que emmagatzemen l'aigua de la pluja a uns trenta metres sota terra. N'hi ha 15, 13 de subterranis i dos a cel obert.

Tenen capacitat d'absorbir prop de 500 milions de litres d'aigua, però en només 24 hores es va superar aquest llindar .

La tinenta d'alcaldia Laia Bonet ha assegurat que si la ciutat ha "sobreviscut" a les pluges és per la xarxa actual.

Un dels dipòsits més grans és el de Joan Miró, on caben 70 milions de litres, l'equivalent a 22 piscines olímpiques. A les columnes, encara es veuen les marques de fins on va arribar l'aigua.

Aquest, juntament amb vuit dipòsits més, va superar la capacitat total d'emmagatzematge entre el 3 d'octubre a les nou del matí i el dia 4 a la mateixa hora.

"Patíem perquè no ens havíem enfrontat mai a una situació tan complicada; el buidatge normalment es fa de forma progressiva i es va haver de fer molt ràpid", ha relatat Ortiz.

La funció principal dels dipòsits és evitar que els carrers s'inundin quan plou. L'aigua de la pluja baixa pel clavegueram fins que entra en "càrrega", un moment perillós perquè és quan pot sobreeixir a la superfície i provocar inundacions.

Abans que passi, l'aigua entra als dipòsits fins que s'atura o afluixa l'episodi de pluja i es poden buidar. Després de passar per una depuradora, part de l'aigua retorna a la xarxa i una altra part s'aboca al mar.

Davant la previsió que cada cop aquests episodis de pluja torrencial siguin més freqüents, Bonet ha defensat que cal "accelerar" l'ampliació de la xarxa.

Ha explicat que l'últim dipòsit pluvial que es va construir va ser el 2013 i ha admès que no n'hi haurà cap de nou fins al 2028, quan entrarà en funcionament el de la rambla Prim .

"Se suma a altres projectes que ja tenim en marxa, com el de Vallcarca, el de la Sagrera i el de Bac de Roda". La previsió del govern és arribar a tenir 29 dipòsits d'aigua .
sources.headline: La pluja de l'octubre omple per primer cop els 15 dipòsits d'aigua de Barcelona: com funcionen
